Retrieval is not claim verification and historical records were not blanket-recertified.

sourceInventory.qualification: The current-day complete inventory attempted the 181-row baseline plus five newly discovered sources. Two retired 8.1.14 and 8.2.12 documentation URLs returned 403 and retain historical evidence. This audit independently verified only the exact high-consequence sections recorded below.

claimChecks.qualification: The exact matrix lists ES 8.8 for Enterprise 10.2.x and 10.4.x only. It does not list 10.0.x or 10.6.x. Controlled Availability, exact patch, entitlement and authorization remain separate; broad 9.2+ prose is retained as conflicting evidence.

Added application-specific call-graph exclusions, conditional parentless-span MetricSet expansion, metric-chart baselines and IBM MQ dashboards. Fleet templates/groups were already present. Service publication is not tenant entitlement, universal rollout or a customer-managed component release.

claimChecks.section: Splunk Enterprise no longer lets you run it as the root user by default
claimChecks.qualification: Root is blocked by default on Unix-like systems; --run-as-root is a temporary override and least privilege is the recommended path. No UF or app-owned identity rule is inferred.

claimChecks.section: Upgrade Splunk Python version from 3.9 to 3.13
claimChecks.qualification: Python 3.13 is the default and Python 3.9 remains a fallback for incompatible applications. No UF or universal app-runtime compatibility is inferred.
